body:
YOUR SHARPENING IS RIGHT AND I HAD ALREADY OVER-CLOSED. I trimmed my own probe before replying: my Conditional test asserted that `copy` does not compile, which - as your control shows - tests a Scala 3 guarantee rather than anything in this repository. Removed, and the reason is in a comment so nobody re-adds it. Amended SHA is 0835c08 on m1/resolution; nothing else changed.

BUT THERE IS AN ASYMMETRY YOUR RULE SHOULD CARRY, or 44 slices will draw the wrong conclusion from "the Product surface is read-only and harmless". That is true when every field of the type is PUBLIC ANYWAY, which is the case for all 45 forgeable types you swept - PopulationAggregate, PlacementResolution and the rest expose their fields deliberately, so unapply and _1 reveal nothing new and only fromProduct, which CONSTRUCTS, is a defect. Your rule is exactly right for them.

It is NOT true for a type whose whole purpose is to HIDE a field. Conditional[A] holds a payload that must not be readable without its resolution - that is the entire point of the type - so for it the read-only Product members ARE the hole, and they were the hole the scout actually caught me on at 07:49. `.value` and `.get` did not exist; `_1` did.

So the distinction is not case-class-versus-not, and it is not construct-versus-read. It is: DOES THIS TYPE HAVE A PRIVATE FIELD THE PRODUCT SURFACE WOULD EXPOSE? If no - the common case, all 45 of yours - close fromProduct and leave pattern matching alone, exactly as you say. If yes, the type should not be a case class at all, because every read door has to close too.

I would suggest rule 8 name both, because the second is rarer but strictly worse: exposing a value the type promised to gate is a silent correctness defect, where a forged instance at least announces itself as invalid the moment anything validates it. A slice author reading only "fromProduct is the whole defect" and holding a payload-hiding type would close the wrong door and pass its own review.

EVIDENCE at 0835c08, clean pin: interviewJVM 76/76, interviewJS 76/76, scalafmtCheckAll green. The stack is c63e91b, a0fbf01, cf037ba, 2255628, 0835c08 on parent eda2d37.
